# Animation

214 tools for Animation Blueprints and state machines, montages, notifies and curves, blend spaces, skeletons and skeletal meshes, IK Rig and retargeting, Control Rig, Pose Search and motion warping.

Back to the [index](README.md).

## `add_anim_composite_segment`

*Additive.*

Add an FAnimSegment that plays a whole UAnimSequence to a UAnimComposite's AnimationTrack in one undo step, re-stack all segments end to end, recompute the composite length and save the asset. The segments are ordered by start_pos before the re-stack, so to append at the end pass start_pos at or past the current composite_length; the default 0 ties with the first segment and normally sorts in front of it. Every call adds another segment (not idempotent). Create the composite first with create_anim_composite, check it with get_anim_asset_info, and take a segment out by index with remove_anim_composite_segment. A composite and sequence on different skeletons, or a path that does not load, is an error and nothing changes. A failed save (always while PIE runs) makes the reply's success false with saved=false and save_error; the success field inside the data stays true, so read saved.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `composite_path` | string | yes | Object path of the UAnimComposite, e.g. '/Game/Animation/AC_Example' (create_anim_composite makes one). |
| `animation_path` | string | yes | Object path of the UAnimSequence to play, on the composite's skeleton, e.g. '/Game/Anims/A_Walk'; the segment covers its full length. |
| `start_pos` | number | no | Start time in seconds used only to order the new segment among the existing ones before all are re-stacked end to end (default 0, which normally sorts it first); pass the current composite_length or more to append. |
| `play_rate` | number | no | Playback rate of the segment, 1.0 = normal speed, 2.0 = twice as fast (default 1.0). |
| `loop_count` | number | no | How many times the segment repeats, a whole number; values below 1 become 1 (default 1). |

**Returns:** `{ composite_path, animation_path, num_segments, composite_length, segments, success, saved, save_error }`

## `add_anim_conduit`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Add a conduit node named conduit_name to an existing state machine of an Animation Blueprint (a missing blueprint or machine is an error; create the machine with add_anim_state_machine), then mark the blueprint structurally modified and save it without compiling. Idempotent by name: an existing conduit is returned unchanged (already_existed true). The conduit is placed unconnected: link it to states with add_anim_transition; remove_anim_conduit undoes it. Refused while PIE runs unless force=true; a failed save is an error, the change kept in memory.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Path to the UAnimBlueprint asset |
| `machine_name` | string | yes | Name of the target state machine |
| `conduit_name` | string | yes | Name for the new conduit |

**Returns:** `{ anim_blueprint_path: string, machine_name: string, conduit_name: string, node_class: string, conduit_created: bool, already_existed: bool, saved: bool, conduit_count: int, save_error?: string }`

## `add_anim_curve_name`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Register a curve name as curve metadata on a USkeleton (USkeleton::AddCurveMetaData) in an undo transaction, then save the skeleton package. Idempotent: a name already registered is a success with added=false, already_existed=true and saved=false, and the skeleton is neither modified nor saved. It adds no keys -- to put a keyed float curve on a UAnimSequence use add_anim_float_curve; remove_anim_curve_name is the inverse. An unknown skeleton is an error and a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `curve_name` | string | yes | The curve name to add (e.g. 'Curve_Example'). |
| `skeleton_path` | string | no | Asset path of the USkeleton to edit (/Game/...); when omitted or empty the engine asset /Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube_Skeleton is edited and saved. |

**Returns:** `{ skeleton_path, curve_name, present, added, already_existed, curve_count, saved, save_error, message }`

## `add_anim_float_curve`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Add a float curve (Editable flag) to a UAnimSequence, or rekey the one already there, through its data controller: its keys become the [time, value] pairs as linear keys with auto tangents, in one undo step, then the package is saved. An existing float curve of that name is kept and its keys are replaced (idempotent); one that already holds exactly those keys is a success with changed=false, applied=false and saved=false, and nothing is written or saved. curve_found confirms the curve and num_keys counts the keys sent. A missing sequence is an error, and so are keys the data controller rejects, with nothing saved; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. curve_type=transform is refused before anything is loaded, since [time, value] keys only fit a float curve. Transform curves: add_anim_transform_curve; a skeleton-only name: add_anim_curve_name; read back: get_anim_curve_data.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UAnimSequence. |
| `curve_name` | string | yes | Float curve name to add or rekey. |
| `keys` | array | no | JSON array of [time, value] pairs, time in seconds (default [[0,0],[1,1]]); entries that are not such a pair are skipped. |
| `curve_type` | string | no | Optional curve type the keys are meant for: float (the default, the only one written). transform is refused with an error pointing at add_anim_transform_curve; any other value is an error. |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, curve_name, num_float_curves, num_keys, curve_found, changed, applied, success, saved, save_error, message }`

## `add_anim_graph_node`

*Additive.*

Place a UAnimGraphNode_* (by class name) into an AnimGraph or a state's inner graph. Saves the ABP but does NOT recompile it -- run compile_anim_blueprint after your edits for runtime effect.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Path or name of the UAnimBlueprint. |
| `node_class` | string | yes | AnimGraphNode class: short name (e.g. "AnimGraphNode_Slot", "AnimGraphNode_PoseSearchHistoryCollector") or full path. |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph; omit/"AnimGraph" for the top-level AnimGraph, or a nested name like "MainSM > Idle". |
| `x` | number | no | Node X position (optional, default 0). |
| `y` | number | no | Node Y position (optional, default 0). |

**Returns:** `{ node_id, node_class, graph_name, pins[], saved } (NodeToJson of the created node)`

## `add_anim_notify`

*Additive.*

Add an instance of a UAnimNotify class at a time on a UAnimSequence notify track (created when missing) and save the sequence; each call adds another event, and an unknown class is an error. Returns time and success. For montages use add_montage_notify; for durations add_anim_notify_state. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `animation_path` | string | yes | Full asset path to the UAnimSequence. |
| `notify_name` | string | yes | Class name of a loaded UAnimNotify subclass, tried as given and then with the AnimNotify_ prefix (e.g. 'AN_Footstep', or "PlaySound" for AnimNotify_PlaySound); a Blueprint notify goes by its generated name ending in _C. |
| `time` | number | no | Notify trigger time in seconds (default 0) |
| `track_name` | string | no | Notify track name (default 'Default') |

**Returns:** `{ animation_path, notify_name, time, success, saved, save_error, message }`

## `add_anim_notify_name`

*Additive.*

Register a notify name in the AnimationNotifies list of a USkeleton inside an undo transaction and save the skeleton package; returns present, notify_count and saved. A name already registered is a success with added=false, already_existed=true and saved=false, and the skeleton is neither modified nor saved. Without skeleton_path it edits /Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube_Skeleton. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Inverse: remove_anim_notify_name.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `notify_name` | string | yes | The notify name to register (e.g. 'Footstep'). |
| `skeleton_path` | string | no | Asset path of the USkeleton to edit (/Game/...); when omitted or empty the engine asset /Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube_Skeleton is edited and saved. |

**Returns:** `{ skeleton_path, notify_name, present, added, already_existed, notify_count, saved, save_error, message }`

*Additive.*

Add an instance of a UAnimNotifyState class with a start time and duration to a UAnimSequence notify track (created when missing) and save the sequence; each call adds another event, and unknown classes are refused. Returns start_time, duration and success. For instant notifies use add_anim_notify. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `animation_path` | string | yes | Full asset path to the UAnimSequence. |
| `notify_state_name` | string | yes | Class name of a loaded UAnimNotifyState subclass, tried as given and then with the AnimNotifyState_ prefix (e.g. "Trail" for AnimNotifyState_Trail); a Blueprint notify state goes by its generated name ending in _C. |
| `start_time` | number | no | Notify state start time in seconds (default 0) |
| `duration` | number | no | Notify state duration in seconds (default 1.0) |
| `track_name` | string | no | Notify track name (default 'Default') |

**Returns:** `{ animation_path, notify_state_name, start_time, duration, success, saved, save_error, message }`

## `add_anim_slot_group`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Add an animation slot group (a named group that montage slots belong to; one slot per group plays at a time) to a USkeleton asset in one undo step and save the skeleton. Use it before giving a montage a slot in a new group; the montage side is create_anim_montage (slot_name) or add_montage_slot, and the inverse is remove_anim_slot_group. get_skeleton_info with load_full_data=true reports slot_group_count. Idempotent: a group that already exists returns added=false and is not changed, but the skeleton is still marked dirty and saved. A skeleton that does not load is an error. A failed save (always while PIE runs) makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Edit a project copy (create_editable_skeleton), not engine content.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeleton_path` | string | yes | USkeleton asset as a package or object path, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SK_Hero_Skeleton", as get_skeleton_info returns it. |
| `group_name` | string | yes | Name of the slot group to add, compared as an FName (case ignored), e.g. "WeaponGroup". |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, group_name: string, added: bool, slot_group_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_anim_state`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Add a state node named state_name to an existing state machine of an Animation Blueprint, then mark the blueprint structurally modified and save it without compiling (compile_anim_blueprint gives runtime effect). Not an undo step. Idempotent by name: a state of that name (case-insensitive) is returned unchanged with already_existed true, and nothing is saved. The machine must sit on the top-level AnimGraph (add_anim_state_machine creates it); a missing blueprint or machine is an error. The new state is unconnected and its animation graph empty: link it with add_anim_transition, fill it with add_anim_graph_node, check the machine with get_anim_state_machine_info; remove_anim_state is the inverse. Refused while PIE runs unless force=true; a failed save is an error, the change kept in memory.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Content path of the UAnimBlueprint (object or package path), e.g. '/Game/Characters/ABP_Hero'. |
| `machine_name` | string | yes | Name of a state machine on the blueprint's top-level AnimGraph, as get_anim_blueprint_info lists it in state_machines (case-insensitive), e.g. 'Locomotion'. |
| `state_name` | string | yes | Name for the new state, e.g. 'Idle'; the reply's state_name is the name its graph actually got. |

**Returns:** `{ anim_blueprint_path: string, machine_name: string, state_name: string, node_class: string, state_created: bool, already_existed: bool, saved: bool, state_count: int, save_error?: string }`

## `add_anim_state_machine`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Add a state machine node named machine_name to the top-level AnimGraph of an Animation Blueprint, then mark the blueprint structurally modified and save it without compiling (compile_anim_blueprint gives runtime effect). Idempotent by name: an existing machine is returned unchanged (already_existed true). The node starts with only its entry and is not connected to the Output Pose: wire it with connect_anim_graph_pins, fill it with add_anim_state, add_anim_conduit and add_anim_transition, or build it in one call with build_anim_state_machine. Refused while PIE runs unless force=true; a failed save is an error, the change kept in memory.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Path to the UAnimBlueprint asset |
| `machine_name` | string | yes | Name for the new state machine |

**Returns:** `{ anim_blueprint_path: string, machine_name: string, node_class: string, state_machine_graph: string, state_machine_created: bool, already_existed: bool, saved: bool, state_machine_count: int, save_error?: string }`

## `add_anim_sync_marker`

*Destructive.*

Append an authored sync marker (name and time, on marker track 0) to a UAnimSequence in an undo transaction and save it; duplicates are not checked, nor is the time checked against the sequence length. Returns num_sync_markers. Remove with remove_anim_sync_marker. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UAnimSequence. |
| `marker_name` | string | yes | Name of the sync marker (e.g. "LeftFootDown"); sequences in one sync group line up markers that share a name. |
| `time` | number | no | Sync marker time in seconds (default 0.5) |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, marker_name, time, num_sync_markers, success, saved, save_error, message }`

## `add_anim_transform_curve`

*Destructive.*

Add a transform curve (RCT_Transform) to a UAnimSequence via the data controller and set its keys as linear keys per axis, in one undo step, then save the package; the sampling rate of the sequence is left as it is. An existing transform curve of that name is kept and its keys are replaced; one that already holds exactly those keys is a success with changed=false, keys_set=false and saved=false, and nothing is written or saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Object path of the UAnimSequence. |
| `curve_name` | string | yes | Name of the transform curve to add. |
| `keys` | array | no | JSON array of {time, location:[x,y,z], rotation:[pitch,yaw,roll], scale:[x,y,z]} objects |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, curve_name, num_transform_curves, num_keys, keys_set, changed, success, saved, save_error, message? }`

## `add_anim_transition`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Add a transition from source_state to target_state in an existing state machine of an Animation Blueprint, set its crossfade, blend mode, bidirectional flag and priority, then mark the blueprint structurally modified and save it without compiling (compile_anim_blueprint gives runtime effect). The machine (top-level AnimGraph) and both endpoints (a state or a conduit) are matched by name without case; a missing one, the same state twice or an unknown blend_mode is an error. Idempotent per pair: an existing source->target transition is returned unchanged with already_existed=true and nothing is saved (to change its settings, remove_anim_transition and add it again). It starts with no rule: wire one with set_anim_transition_rule_from_bool, set_anim_transition_rule_from_comparison or set_anim_transition_rule_automatic. Refused while PIE runs unless force=true; a failed save is an error, the change kept in memory.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Path to the UAnimBlueprint asset |
| `machine_name` | string | yes | Name of the state machine that owns both states |
| `source_state` | string | yes | Name of the source state or conduit (transition origin), matched without case |
| `target_state` | string | yes | Name of the target state or conduit (transition destination), matched without case |
| `crossfade_duration` | number | no | Optional blend duration in seconds (default 0.2) |
| `blend_mode` | string | no | Optional EAlphaBlendOption name, e.g. Linear, Cubic, HermiteCubic (default HermiteCubic); an unknown name is an error |
| `bidirectional` | boolean | no | Optional, default false; sets the Bidirectional flag so the same transition can also fire target->source (no second transition is added) |
| `priority_order` | number | no | Optional priority order (default 1); when several transitions out of a state pass at once, the smallest value wins |

**Returns:** `{ anim_blueprint_path: string, machine_name: string, source_state: string, target_state: string, transition_created: bool, already_existed: bool, crossfade_duration: number, blend_mode: string, bidirectional: bool, priority_order: int, transition_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_animation_asset_to_pose_search_database`

*Additive.*

Append an animation asset to a UPoseSearchDatabase as an enabled entry over its full range, then save the database; an asset already in it is left alone (already_existed=true, saved=false, nothing saved). The asset type is not checked, and the search index is not rebuilt: run build_pose_search_database_index afterwards.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `database_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UPoseSearchDatabase (required). |
| `animation_asset_path` | string | yes | Asset path of a UAnimSequenceBase / UAnimComposite / UAnimMontage / UBlendSpace (required). |

**Returns:** `{ database_path, animation_asset_path, animation_asset_count, added, already_existed, saved, message }`

## `add_blend_space_sample`

*Additive.*

Add one sample (an animation placed at a blend position) to a UBlendSpace or UBlendSpace1D in one undo step, rebuild its runtime data and save the asset. Every call appends a new sample, so it is not a retry-safe call. A sample the engine would reject is refused before anything changes, with success=false, added=false, sample_index -1, saved=false and the reason in the error: an animation whose skeleton is neither the blend space's nor compatible with it, an additive type the blend space does not take or that differs from the existing samples', a position already taken by a sample, or a position an axis cannot widen to in 1000 grid steps or fewer. Otherwise a position past an axis range widens that axis. The sample is read back after the rebuild: animation and blend_x, blend_y, blend_z are what the asset holds at sample_index. Create the asset with create_blend_space and list its samples with get_blend_space_samples; move or swap an existing sample with set_blend_space_sample, and take one out with remove_blend_space_sample. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blendspace_path` | string | yes | Object path of the UBlendSpace or UBlendSpace1D asset, e.g. '/Game/Animation/BS_Locomotion' (create_blend_space makes one). |
| `animation_path` | string | yes | Object path of the UAnimSequence played at this position, on the blend space's skeleton or one compatible with it, e.g. '/Game/Animation/Run_Fwd'. |
| `blend_value` | any | no | Blend position in the axis units: one number for a 1D blend space, or [x, y] (up to 3 numbers) for a 2D one, e.g. [0, 300]; default 0 on every axis. |

**Returns:** `{ blendspace_path: string, sample_index: int, num_samples: int, added: bool, animation?: string, blend_x?: number, blend_y?: number, blend_z?: number, saved: bool, save_error?: string, message?: string }`

## `add_bone`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Add a bone named bone_name to the reference skeleton of a USkeleton asset under parent_name (omitted or empty: an extra root bone), with local_transform relative to the parent (a zero or missing scale becomes 1), then save the skeleton. Idempotent by name: an existing bone is returned (added false, already_existed true) without checking its parent or saving. An unknown parent is an error, and so is a failed save. Only the skeleton changes: skeletal meshes using it get no new bone, and there is no undo entry. No commit_bone_changes is needed; set_bone_parent and set_bone_transform edit bones, add_virtual_bone adds virtual ones.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeleton_path` | string | yes | Path to the USkeleton asset |
| `bone_name` | string | yes | Name for the new bone; when a bone of that name already exists nothing changes (added false) |
| `parent_name` | string | no | Parent bone name, or empty/null for a new root bone |
| `local_transform` | object | no | Optional {location:[x,y,z], rotation:[p,y,r], scale:[x,y,z]}, defaults to identity |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path, bone_name, bone_index, parent_index, bone_count, added, already_existed, saved, op: "add_bone" }`

## `add_foot_ik_node`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Add a Leg IK node (UAnimGraphNode_LegIK) to the top-level AnimGraph of an Animation Blueprint, or reuse the first one already there, bind the feet into its LegsDefinition, then mark the blueprint structurally modified and save it without compiling. Leg 0 gets left_foot_bone and leg 1 right_foot_bone as the FK foot bone; a leg's IK target bone is set to the same bone when it is unset or the leg's foot changes, so the node compiles but has no effect until each IK target names an IK bone (set_anim_graph_node_property on LegsDefinition with the returned node_id); legs beyond the first two and the other leg settings are kept. Bones the target skeleton lacks are an error and nothing is written. The node is left unwired: connect it with connect_anim_graph_pins. Idempotent; refused while PIE runs unless force=true.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Path to the UAnimBlueprint asset. |
| `left_foot_bone` | string | yes | Left foot bone, written as the FK foot bone of leg 0; checked against the target skeleton when the blueprint has one. |
| `right_foot_bone` | string | yes | Right foot bone, written as the FK foot bone of leg 1; checked against the target skeleton when the blueprint has one. |

**Returns:** `{ anim_blueprint_path, node_id, left_foot_bone, right_foot_bone, legs: [{ fk_foot_bone, ik_foot_bone, num_bones_in_limb }], bones_checked_against, ik_node_count, already_existed, saved, save_error }`

## `add_ik_goal`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Add an IK goal to an IK Rig, associated with a bone, through the IK Rig controller (one undo transaction), then save the asset.  If bone_name is omitted, a leaf bone of the rig's skeletal mesh is picked automatically. Idempotent: a goal of that name on the same bone is not re-created but returned with already_exists=true, saved=false and a note, and nothing is saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UIKRigDefinition asset |
| `goal_name` | string | yes | Unique name for the new goal |
| `bone_name` | string | no | Optional bone name to attach the goal to |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, goal_name: string, bone_name: string, goal_count: int, saved: bool, already_exists?: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `add_ik_retarget_chain`

*Additive.*

Add a retarget bone chain from start_bone to end_bone, optionally tied to an IK goal, to an IK Rig asset and save it. Both bones must exist in the skeleton of the rig; the chain name is made unique, so read chain_name back. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | IK Rig (UIKRigDefinition) asset path, e.g. "/Game/Retarget/IK_Hero". |
| `chain_name` | string | yes | Name for the new retarget chain (uniquified by the engine) |
| `start_bone` | string | yes | First bone of the chain; must exist in the skeleton of the rig. |
| `end_bone` | string | yes | Last bone of the chain; must exist in the skeleton of the rig. |
| `goal_name` | string | no | IK goal to attach the chain to (default none); not checked against the goals of the rig. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, chain_name: string, start_bone: string, end_bone: string, goal_name: string, chain_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_ik_solver`

*Additive.*

Add a new, unconfigured IK solver at the bottom of an existing IK Rig's solver stack through the IK Rig controller (one undo step), then save the asset. Every call adds another solver (not idempotent); solver_index in the reply is the handle the other solver tools take. Create the rig first with create_ik_rig; then set its bones with set_ik_solver_bones, its settings with set_ik_solver_settings, attach goals (add_ik_goal) with connect_ik_goal_to_solver, reorder with move_ik_solver_in_stack, take one out with remove_ik_solver, and read the stack back with get_ik_rig_info or one solver with get_ik_solver_details. An unknown solver_type, or a rig that does not load, is an error and nothing changes. A failed save (always while PIE runs) makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, the solver kept in memory.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | IK Rig (UIKRigDefinition) asset as a package or object path, e.g. "/Game/Rigs/IK_Mannequin". |
| `solver_type` | string | no | "FullBodyIK" (default; also "FBIK"), "Limb", "Pole", "BodyMover", "SetTransform" or "StretchLimb", case ignored; spaced forms ("Full Body IK") and the struct names ("FIKRigLimbSolver") are accepted too. solver_type in the reply is the canonical name and solver_struct the engine struct. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, solver_index: int, solver_type: string, solver_struct: string, solver_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_montage_section`

*Additive.*

Add a composite section to a UAnimMontage at an absolute start time, or move the existing section of that name there; it does not link sections (use link_montage_sections). Saves the montage in an undo transaction and returns start_time, section_count, sections, already_existed and added (true only for a new section). A section of that name already at that start time is a success with changed=false and saved=false, and the montage is neither modified nor saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `montage_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the montage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example'). |
| `section_name` | string | yes | Name of the section to add (e.g. 'Loop'). |
| `start_time` | number | no | Absolute section start time in seconds (default 0) |

**Returns:** `{ montage_path, section_name, start_time, section_count, sections, already_existed, added, changed, saved, save_error, message }`

## `add_montage_segment`

*Additive.*

Append an animation segment referencing a real UAnimSequence to a montage slot. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Inverse: remove_montage_segment; read: get_montage_info.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `montage_path` | string | yes | Object path of the UAnimMontage (e.g. "/Game/MyGame/AM_Example"). |
| `anim_sequence_path` | string | yes | Object path of the UAnimSequence to reference. |
| `slot_name` | string | no | Montage slot name (e.g. DefaultSlot) |
| `play_rate` | number | no | Segment play rate (default 1.0) |
| `loop_count` | number | no | Segment loop count, minimum 1 (default 1) |

**Returns:** `{ montage_path, anim_sequence_path, slot_name, segment_count, montage_length, play_rate, loop_count, success, saved, save_error }`

## `add_montage_slot`

*Additive.*

Add an empty slot animation track with the given slot name to a UAnimMontage in an undo transaction and save it; an existing slot of that name is a success with added=false, already_existed=true and saved=false, and the montage is neither modified nor saved. Returns slot_count, the slots list and present. Fill it with add_montage_segment; inverse: remove_montage_slot. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `montage_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the montage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example'). |
| `slot_name` | string | yes | Name of the slot track to add (e.g. 'UpperBody'). |

**Returns:** `{ montage_path, slot_name, slot_count, slots, present, already_existed, added, saved, save_error, message }`

## `add_motion_warping_component`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Attach a UMotionWarpingComponent named MotionWarping to an editor-world actor given by full object path, internal name or label. add_component_to_actor (component_type MotionWarpingComponent, idempotent=true) does the same for an actor's internal name only; this tool adds the path/label lookup. Idempotent: if the actor already has one, it is returned with already_existed:true and nothing is written. A new one is an instance component (save_level keeps it, and construction-script reruns do not drop it) added in one undo step; the actor's package is marked dirty, not saved. When another object of the actor already holds the name MotionWarping, the new component gets a unique variant, returned in component_name. Add targets with add_motion_warping_target, read them with get_motion_warping_component_info.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_path` | string | yes | Full editor path (e.g. "/Game/Maps/Test.Test:PersistentLevel.ActorName"), internal name or label of the actor. |

**Returns:** `{ actor_path: string, component_name: string, component_path: string, already_existed: bool }`

## `add_motion_warping_target`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Add (or update in-place) a FMotionWarpingTarget on an existing UMotionWarpingComponent, including moving or re-aiming an existing target. Exactly one of four payload shapes must be supplied: (1) component_path -> AddOrUpdateWarpTargetFromComponent(name, comp, NAME_None, false, TargetsForwardVector, ZeroVector, ZeroRotator); (2) location + rotation -> AddOrUpdateWarpTargetFromLocationAndRotation; (3) location only -> AddOrUpdateWarpTargetFromLocation (rotation [0,0,0]); (4) rotation only, on a target that already exists -> its Location is kept and only the rotation changes (a missing target is an error). Shapes 2-4 rebuild the target as a plain transform target, so a component-based one loses its Component, BoneName, follow flag and offsets. The engine API is idempotent by WarpTargetName (replace-in-place). Marks the owning level dirty; WarpTargets is Transient, so the targets are not saved with the level.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_path` | string | yes | Full editor path or short name of the actor. actor_name (the internal object name) is accepted as an alias. |
| `target_name` | string | yes | FName identifier for the warp target. warp_target_name is accepted as an alias. |
| `location` | array | no | Optional world [x, y, z] location for the target. |
| `rotation` | array | no | Optional world [pitch, yaw, roll] rotation in degrees for the target; alone, it re-aims an existing target and keeps its location. |
| `component_path` | string | no | Optional name of a USceneComponent on the actor to drive the target transform. |
| `warp_target_name` | string | no |   |
| `actor_name` | string | no |   |

**Returns:** `{ actor_path: string, target_name: string, warp_target_count: int, previous_count: int, source: string (component | location_and_rotation | location | rotation), already_existed: bool, previous_location?: [x,y,z], previous_rotation?: [pitch,yaw,roll], location: [x,y,z], rotation: [pitch,yaw,roll], changed: bool }`

## `add_notify_track`

*Additive.*

Add a named notify TRACK to a UAnimSequence (the track itself, not events on it) in an undo transaction and save it. A track of that name already there is a success with already_existed=true and nothing saved; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `animation_path` | string | yes | Full asset path to the UAnimSequence. |
| `track_name` | string | yes | Notify track name to add. |
| `color` | string | no | Optional track color as an [r,g,b] or [r,g,b,a] float array (default white). |

**Returns:** `{ animation_path, track_name, track_names, track_count, already_existed, saved, save_error, message }`

## `add_pose_search_channel_to_schema`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Add a feature channel (what motion matching compares: Pose, Trajectory, Position, Velocity or Heading) to a Pose Search schema, or, when the schema already has a channel of that class, set that channel's weight instead (already_existed true), then re-finalize the schema and save it. Use it to shape what a database built on the schema matches on; remove one with remove_pose_search_channel_from_schema, read the result with get_pose_search_schema_info, and rebuild the index afterwards with build_pose_search_database_index, which this does not do. Idempotent per channel class: the check looks at every channel the schema has, finalized or not, so a repeat call never adds a duplicate. finalized says whether the schema finalized with the change: when false (schema_cardinality 0, a finalize_warning, usually a channel naming a bone the skeleton lacks) the channel is still added and saved, but the schema cannot be built until that is fixed. An unknown channel_type or a schema that does not load is an error and nothing changes; a failed save answers success false with the change kept in memory.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schema_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UPoseSearchSchema (required). |
| `channel_type` | string | yes | One of 'Pose', 'Trajectory', 'Position', 'Velocity', 'Heading' (required). |
| `weight` | number | no | How much this channel counts against the others when matching, a float >= 0 (default 1.0); omitting it on an existing channel resets that channel's weight to 1.0. |

**Returns:** `{ schema_path, channel_type, channel_class, weight, schema_cardinality, channel_count (finalized), source_channel_count, finalized, finalize_warning?, added, already_existed, weight_updated, saved, save_error?, message }`

## `add_pose_to_pose_asset`

*Destructive.*

Add a pose copied from the skeleton reference pose to a UPoseAsset under the given name (a pose of that name is replaced) in an undo transaction and save it; refused when the asset has no skeleton. A pose of that name that already holds exactly that reference pose (every bone a track, zero curve values, no source animation GUID) is a success with added=false, already_existed=true and saved=false, and the asset is neither modified nor saved. Returns num_poses, num_tracks and already_existed. For poses from animation frames use create_pose_asset_from_anim_sequence. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pose_asset_path` | string | yes | Path to the UPoseAsset (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/Pose_Example'). |
| `pose_name` | string | yes | Name of the pose to add (e.g. 'RefPose_A'). |

**Returns:** `{ pose_asset_path, pose_name, num_poses, num_tracks, present, added, already_existed, saved, save_error, message }`

## `add_retargeter_op`

*Additive.*

Add a retarget op to the op stack of an IK Retargeter asset through its controller (one undo transaction), then save the asset; op_index and op_name are where and how the engine placed it. Default type: FK Chains op. An unknown op type, or a singleton op type the stack already has, is an error. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_retargeter_path` | string | yes | Path to the UIKRetargeter asset |
| `op_type` | string | no | Optional op class path (default "/Script/IKRig.IKRetargetFKChainsOp") |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, op_index: int, op_name: string, op_type: string, op_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_rig_element`

*Additive.*

Add a bone, a null (a space: a transform-only element) or an animation control to the hierarchy of a Control Rig Blueprint, under parent_name or at the root, then compile and save the blueprint; there is no undo step and it is refused while PIE runs unless force is set. element_type picks the kind: a bone or null is placed at location/rotation/scale in rig global space; a control (control_type, Float by default) gets a zero or identity value and no limits, its name doubling as its display name, and an unrecognised control_type makes a Float control with control_type_recognized false instead of failing. The engine keeps names unique, so element_key is the name the element really got (a name in use gets a numbered suffix, so each call adds another element), and parent is the parent read back from the hierarchy. A parent the hierarchy does not have is an error and nothing is added; so is a rig that cannot be loaded, and a failed save makes success false with save_error. Set a control up with set_rig_control_value, set_rig_control_limits and set_rig_control_settings; inspect: get_rig_hierarchy; rename or take out: rename_rig_element, remove_rig_element.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `control_rig_path` | string | yes | Control Rig Blueprint asset path, e.g. "/Game/Rigs/CR_Hero" |
| `element_name` | string | yes | Name of the new element. bone_name, null_name and control_name are accepted as aliases. |
| `element_type` | string | no | Optional. "bone" (default), "null" ("space" is accepted) or "control", case ignored; defaults to "control" when control_type is given. Any other value is an error. |
| `control_type` | string | no | Optional, controls only: one of "bool", "float", "scalefloat", "integer", "int", "vector2d", "position", "scale", "rotator", "transform", "eulertransform" (default "float"). Given with element_type bone or null it is an error. |
| `parent_name` | string | no | Existing element to parent the new one under; omitted or empty puts it at the root, and a name the hierarchy lacks is an error. A bone is parented under a bone only. |
| `parent_type` | string | no | Optional element type of the parent for a null or control ("Bone"/"Null"/"Control"/etc, case ignored, "Space" means Null); default Bone for a null and Null for a control, and an unknown type falls back to that default. Bones ignore it. |
| `location` | array | no | Optional [x, y, z] location in rig global space for a bone or null (default the origin). |
| `rotation` | array | no | Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] rotation in rig global space for a bone or null. |
| `scale` | array | no | Optional [x, y, z] scale for a bone or null (default 1,1,1). |
| `bone_name` | string | no |   |
| `null_name` | string | no |   |
| `control_name` | string | no |   |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, element_key: string, element_type: string, parent: string, control_type?: string, control_type_recognized?: bool, bone_count: int, null_count: int, control_count: int, curve_count: int, other_count: int, total: int, saved: bool, save_error: string }`

## `add_rigvm_link`

*Destructive.*

Link an output pin to an input pin in the main RigVM graph of a Control Rig Blueprint (URigVMController::AddLink with its undo, as the editor links, so a new link is one undo step); a link already into that input pin, into a pin inside it or into the pin it is part of, or out of an execute output pin, is replaced. Pins are NodeName.PinName paths as get_rigvm_graph lists them. A new link is then compiled and saved; a failed link (pins missing, incompatible or already linked) is an error with linked and saved false, the graph is left as it was (links the attempt broke are restored), nothing is compiled or saved, and the package keeps the dirty flag it had; should the graph still differ from before, the error says so and the package stays dirty. Refused during PIE unless force. Add nodes with add_rigvm_node and set unlinked inputs with set_rigvm_pin_default; Blueprint graphs use connect_pins. Inverse: remove_rigvm_link.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `control_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the UControlRigBlueprint asset |
| `source_pin` | string | yes | Output pin path NodeA.PinName |
| `target_pin` | string | yes | Input pin path NodeB.PinName |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, source_pin: string, target_pin: string, linked: bool, link_count: int, saved: bool, save_error: string }`

## `add_rigvm_node`

*Additive.*

Add a rig-unit node of node_type to the main RigVM graph of a Control Rig Blueprint loaded by asset path, at position (default 0, 0), then compile and save the rig. Types match case-insensitively (ForwardsSolve means BeginExecution, Setup means PrepareForExecution); any other is an error. node_name is only a request: a taken name gets a unique suffix (the reply has the real one), and every call adds one more node. An event node the graph already has (BeginExecution, PrepareForExecution) is not added twice: when node_name is its name the call succeeds with already_exists=true and saved=false, nothing compiled or saved, otherwise it is an error. A failed save makes success false with save_error, the node kept in memory. Refused during PIE unless force=true. Next: add_rigvm_link to wire it, set_rigvm_pin_default for inputs, get_rigvm_graph for pin paths; the inverse is remove_rigvm_node.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `control_rig_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UControlRigBlueprint, e.g. "/Game/Rigs/CR_Mannequin". |
| `node_type` | string | yes | BeginExecution, PrepareForExecution, GetTransform, SetTransform, AimBone, or TwoBoneIKSimple |
| `node_name` | string | no | Optional node name to ask for; defaults to the rig-unit struct name, and a name already in the graph gets a unique suffix. |
| `position` | array | no | Optional [x, y] editor graph position |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, node_name: string, node_title: string, node_type: string, pin_count: int, node_count: int, saved: bool, already_exists: bool, save_error: string }`

## `add_skeletal_mesh_lod`

*Additive.*

Append one LOD to a skeletal mesh asset found by content path, its LOD info a copy of LOD 0's (build and reduction settings, material map, flags) with ScreenSize.Default set to screen_size, or 0.5 when omitted. Each call appends another LOD (not idempotent), in one undo step; the mesh is marked dirty but not saved, and its render data is not regenerated: bake_skeletal_mesh_lod with regenerate_even_if_imported=true and new_lod_count omitted builds the new LOD (its defaults skip it, as it copies LOD 0's imported flag; note says which applies), then keep it with save_asset. A mesh that does not load is an error. To append reduced LODs in one call, use bake_skeletal_mesh_lod with a higher new_lod_count instead. Tune this LOD with set_skeletal_mesh_lod_reduction_settings or set_skeletal_mesh_lod_settings (screen_size); take one out with remove_skeletal_mesh_lod; inspect it with get_skeletal_mesh_lod_info.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SKM_Hero" |
| `screen_size` | number | no | Optional ScreenSize.Default of the new LOD, the screen size at which it switches in (default 0.5); not clamped |

**Returns:** `{ skeletal_mesh_path: string, lod_index: int, lod_count: int, screen_size: float, added: bool, note: string }`

## `add_skeletal_mesh_socket`

*Additive.*

Add a socket on a named bone of a skeletal mesh asset (undoable) and save the mesh. A copy also goes to the mesh's skeleton, which is then saved too; when the skeleton already has a socket of that name, the mesh has no skeleton, or the skeleton is engine content or under a read-only root, no copy is made (added_to_skeleton false) and skeleton_note says why. Errors, writing nothing, when the mesh does not load, the mesh already has a socket of that name, or the bone is missing from the mesh or its skeleton. success is false when a changed package fails to save. Edit existing sockets with set_skeletal_mesh_socket_transform or rename_skeletal_mesh_socket; skeleton-only sockets with add_skeleton_socket.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset |
| `socket_name` | string | yes | Name for the new socket; leading and trailing spaces are trimmed, and a name the mesh already has is an error. |
| `bone_name` | string | yes | Name of the bone to attach the socket to; it must exist in the mesh and, when the copy goes to the skeleton, in the skeleton too. |
| `location` | array | no | Optional [x, y, z] relative location |
| `rotation` | array | no | Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] relative rotation |

**Returns:** `{ socket_name: string, bone_name: string, socket_count: int, location_x: float, location_y: float, location_z: float, added_to_skeleton: bool, skeleton_path: string, skeleton_note: string?, saved: bool, save_error: string?, skeleton_saved: bool?, skeleton_save_error: string? }`

## `add_skeleton_socket`

*Additive.*

Add a socket to a USkeleton asset on a bone (the root by default) at a bone-relative location and rotation, then save; an existing socket of that name is updated in place (already_existed true). A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. A socket on a skeletal mesh asset (copied to its skeleton when that skeleton is project content): add_skeletal_mesh_socket.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeleton_path` | string | yes | USkeleton asset path, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SK_Hero_Skeleton". |
| `socket_name` | string | yes | Name of the socket; an existing socket with this name is updated instead of duplicated. |
| `bone_name` | string | no | Bone to attach the socket to; must exist in the skeleton (default the root bone). |
| `location` | array | no | Socket location relative to its bone as [x, y, z] (default 0,0,0) |
| `rotation` | array | no | Socket rotation relative to its bone as [pitch, yaw, roll] (default 0,0,0) |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, socket_name: string, bone_name: string, socket_count: int, added: bool, already_existed: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string? }`

## `add_virtual_bone`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Add a virtual bone from source_bone to target_bone to a USkeleton asset loaded by asset path, then save the skeleton; the engine names it "VB &lt;source>_&lt;target>", returned as virtual_bone_name. An omitted source_bone is the first bone of the reference skeleton (usually the root) and an omitted target_bone the first other bone. Bone names are not checked against the skeleton, so a misspelt one is stored as given; the same bone for both, or a skeleton with fewer than 2 bones, is an error. Idempotent: a virtual bone that already joins that exact pair is returned with already_exists=true and saved=false, nothing written. A failed save (PIE running, read-only file) makes success false with save_error, the bone kept in memory. Inverse: remove_virtual_bone; list them: get_skeleton_info (load_full_data=true); a project copy to edit: create_editable_skeleton.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeleton_path` | string | yes | USkeleton asset path, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SK_Hero_Skeleton". |
| `source_bone` | string | no | Bone the virtual bone starts from (default the first bone, usually the root); not validated. |
| `target_bone` | string | no | Bone the virtual bone points to (default the first bone that differs from source_bone); not validated. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, virtual_bone_name: string, source_bone: string, target_bone: string, virtual_bone_count: int, saved: bool, already_exists: bool }`

## `assign_skeletal_mesh_physics_asset`

*Destructive.*

Assign a physics asset to a skeletal mesh (or pass null/empty to clear it).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset |
| `physics_asset_path` | string | no | Content path to the physics asset (e.g. /Game/MyPhysAsset); empty string clears the assignment |

**Returns:** `{ skeletal_mesh_path: string, physics_asset_path: string, assigned: bool, cleared: bool, physics_asset_name: string }`

## `bake_skeletal_mesh_lod`

*Destructive.*

Regenerate the LODs of a skeletal mesh asset (found by content path) with the engine's mesh reduction, driven by each LOD's reduction settings, then rebuild its render data; nothing is saved, so follow with save_asset. A new_lod_count below the current count drops the LODs above it; above it, appends reduced LODs up to that count; 0, omitted or equal re-reduces the LODs that were generated, plus imported LODs above 0 with regenerate_even_if_imported and LOD 0 with generate_base_lod. A mesh that does not load is an error; during PIE, where the engine regenerates nothing, the call is refused before the mesh is touched, and any other run the engine refuses fails with baked=false and bake_warning. Author the settings first with set_skeletal_mesh_lod_reduction_settings; one empty LOD entry: add_skeletal_mesh_lod; one LOD out by index: remove_skeletal_mesh_lod; triangle counts: get_asset_lod_settings.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | yes | Content path to the skeletal mesh asset, e.g. "/Game/Characters/SKM_Hero" |
| `new_lod_count` | number | no | Target LOD count; fewer than now drops the extra LODs, more appends reduced ones, and &lt;= 0 (the default when omitted) keeps the current count and re-runs reduction |
| `regenerate_even_if_imported` | boolean | no | bool, also re-reduce imported LODs above 0 when the count is kept (default false) |
| `generate_base_lod` | boolean | no | bool, re-derive LOD 0 from its reduction settings when the count is kept (default false) |

**Returns:** `{ skeletal_mesh_path: string, old_lod_count: int, new_lod_count: int, lod_count: int, baked: bool, regenerate_even_if_imported: bool, generate_base_lod: bool, bake_warning?: string }`

## `build_anim_state_machine`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Atomic JSON-spec builder for an Animation Blueprint state machine. Builds (or reuses) the state machine, then iterates states, transitions, and per-transition rules in one idempotent call. Replaces 8+ primitive cmds (add_anim_state_machine + add_anim_state + add_anim_transition + set_anim_transition_rule_*) with a single spec. Re-running with the same spec is a no-op (each primitive is internally idempotent: state-by-name, transition-by-source+target). For repeated invocations that change rule shape, the rule is re-applied on the existing transition.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Path to the UAnimBlueprint asset |
| `state_machine_name` | string | yes | Target state machine name (created if missing via add_anim_state_machine) |
| `spec` | object | yes | JSON describing the graph shape. states: [{name: str, animation?: str (/Game/Anim/Foo — optional; load-bearing for the runtime state asset but NOT created here), loop?: bool, pos?: [x, y]}]. transitions: [{from: str, to: str, blend?: number (= crossfade_duration seconds), bidirectional?: bool, priority_order?: int, rule?: object}]. Each rule variant maps 1:1 to an existing primitive cmd: {type: "automatic", enabled?: bool = false, trigger_time?: number = 0.0} \| {type: "bool", variable: str (must exist on the AnimBP), invert?: bool = false} \| {type: "comparison", variable: str (must be float/double on the AnimBP), operator: "=="\|"!="\|">"\|"&lt;"\|">="\|"&lt;=", comparison_value: number}. An absent rule leaves the transition inert (no rule wired). |
| `compile_after` | boolean | no | Optional, default false; if true runs compile_anim_blueprint at the end |

**Returns:** `{ success: bool, anim_blueprint_path: string, machine_name: string, machine_already_existed: bool, states_created: int, states_skipped: int, transitions_created: int, transitions_updated: int, transitions_skipped: int, errors: [string], compiled: bool, compiled_after: bool }`

## `build_pose_search_database_index`

*Destructive.*

Start a fresh build of the motion-matching search index of a UPoseSearchDatabase (FAsyncPoseSearchDatabasesManagement::RequestAsyncBuildIndex with NewRequest), cancelling any build already running for it and replacing the old index, and by default wait for it to finish. Run it after add_animation_asset_to_pose_search_database, remove_animation_asset_from_pose_search_database, set_pose_search_database_schema or a schema channel change, none of which rebuild the index; then test it with evaluate_pose_search_query. The index is derived data, not saved into the asset: nothing is saved and there is no undo step. A database that does not load, has no schema (set_pose_search_database_schema), or whose schema still has no finalized channels after a re-finalize in memory is an error before any build. status says what happened: built (success true), in_progress (success true when wait_for_completion is false, since the build was started; a build still running after a wait is a failure), or failed (success false: a database with no animation assets always fails, because the engine fails an empty index, and the message says so; any other failure is in LogPoseSearch). Repeating the call rebuilds again.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `database_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UPoseSearchDatabase, e.g. "/Game/Anim/PSD_Locomotion", as create_pose_search_database returns it (required). |
| `wait_for_completion` | boolean | no | true (default) blocks until the build ends, pumping the engine meanwhile, so large databases take a while; false returns at once, usually with status in_progress (or built when the index was already up to date). |

**Returns:** `{ database_path, schema_path, schema_cardinality, animation_asset_count, wait_for_completion, result: "Success"|"InProgress"|"Failed", status: "built"|"in_progress"|"failed", success, in_progress, failed, message }`

## `clear_anim_graph_node_pin_binding`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Remove the property binding from one input pin of an AnimGraph node (inverse of set_anim_graph_node_pin_binding), dropping a stale binding without recreating the node. Returns was_bound, is_bound and cleared; an unbound pin gives cleared=false, not an error. Undoable; saves the AnimBP without recompiling (run compile_anim_blueprint).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `node_id` | string | yes | NodeGuid of the target UAnimGraphNode_* (from get_graph_nodes). |
| `pin_name` | string | yes | The bound property/pin name whose binding to clear (e.g. "TransformTrajectory"). |
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | no | Path or name of the UAnimBlueprint (aliases: anim_blueprint, blueprint_name). |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph (optional; deep-resolved; default the top-level AnimGraph). |
| `anim_blueprint` | string | no | Alias of anim_blueprint_path, used only when anim_blueprint_path is absent or empty. |
| `blueprint_name` | string | no | Alias of anim_blueprint_path, used only when anim_blueprint_path and anim_blueprint are both absent or empty. |

**Returns:** `{ node_id, pin_name, was_bound, is_bound, cleared, saved }`

## `clear_anim_transition_rule`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Empty the rule of one transition (source_state to target_state) in an Animation Blueprint state machine: every rule-graph node but the result node is deleted, then the blueprint is marked structurally modified and saved without compiling (compile_anim_blueprint). The transition and its settings stay; with nothing wired it is never taken unless its automatic rule is on (set_anim_transition_rule_automatic). Not an undo step. An already empty rule is a success with removed_count 0, nothing saved; a missing blueprint, machine, state or transition is an error. No need to clear first for a new rule: set_anim_transition_rule_from_bool and set_anim_transition_rule_from_comparison rebuild it; remove_anim_transition drops the whole transition. Refused while PIE runs unless force=true; a failed save is an error, the change kept in memory.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Content path of the UAnimBlueprint (object or package path), e.g. '/Game/Characters/ABP_Hero'. |
| `machine_name` | string | yes | Name of a state machine on the blueprint's top-level AnimGraph, as get_anim_blueprint_info lists it in state_machines (case-insensitive), e.g. 'Locomotion'. |
| `source_state` | string | yes | Name of the state or conduit the transition leaves, as get_anim_state_machine_info lists it (case-insensitive), e.g. 'Idle'. |
| `target_state` | string | yes | Name of the state or conduit the transition enters (case-insensitive), e.g. 'Run'. |

**Returns:** `{ anim_blueprint_path, machine_name, source_state, target_state, rule_cleared, already_clear?, sink_present, removed_count, remaining_rule_nodes, saved, save_error? }`

## `collapse_montage_segments`

*Destructive.*

Collapse a montage slot track's segments end-to-end (FAnimTrack::CollapseAnimSegments: no gaps, order preserved) in an undo transaction and save the montage. Segments already end-to-end are a success with applied=false and saved=false, and the montage is neither modified nor saved. An unknown slot is an error. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `montage_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the montage (e.g. '/Game/MyGame/AM_Example'). |
| `slot_name` | string | yes | Name of the slot track to collapse. |

**Returns:** `{ montage_path, slot_name, segment_count, applied, saved, save_error, message }`

## `commit_bone_changes`

*Destructive.*

Mark a skeleton dirty + save it. YOU DO NOT NEED THIS after add_bone / remove_bone / rename_bone / set_bone_transform: each of those already notifies the skeleton's listeners on its own. It exists for the cases those do not cover -- batched mutations made outside the modifier, or an asset import that never went through one (interop with other tools).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skeleton_path` | string | yes | Path to the USkeleton asset |
| `force` | boolean | no | If true, mark dirty and save even when no-op (default true) |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path, committed, force, bone_count, saved, op: "commit_bone_changes" }`

## `compile_anim_blueprint`

*Destructive.*

Compile an Animation Blueprint synchronously and save its package, even when the compile fails; returns status (EBlueprintStatus name), is_up_to_date, has_error and the error and warning messages with their counts. Refused while PIE runs unless force=true. Use get_anim_blueprint_info to inspect without compiling.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Path to the UAnimBlueprint asset |

**Returns:** `{ anim_blueprint_path: string, compiled: bool, status: string, is_up_to_date: bool, has_error: bool, error_count: int, warning_count: int, errors: [string], warnings: [string], saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `connect_anim_graph_pins`

*Destructive.*

Wire two AnimGraph pins (pose links AND data pins) using the graph's OWN schema. USE THIS INSTEAD OF connect_pins inside an AnimGraph: the generic connect_pins uses the K2 schema, which does not understand FPoseLink/FComponentSpacePoseLink pose pins, whereas this goes through UAnimationGraphSchema::TryCreateConnection so pose links connect correctly. Saves the ABP but does NOT recompile it -- run compile_anim_blueprint after your edits for runtime effect.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Path/name of the UAnimBlueprint. |
| `source_node_id` | string | yes | NodeGuid of the source node. |
| `source_pin` | string | yes | Output pin name on the source node. |
| `target_node_id` | string | yes | NodeGuid of the target node. |
| `target_pin` | string | yes | Input pin name on the target node. |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph (optional, default the top-level AnimGraph). |

**Returns:** `{ connected, source_node_id, target_node_id, saved }`

## `connect_ik_goal_to_solver`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Connect an existing IK Rig goal to a solver, creating that solver's per-goal effector/settings, in one undo transaction, then save the asset.  This is the step that makes get_/set_ik_goal_settings work: a goal added via add_ik_goal is not attached to any solver until connected. Idempotent: re-connecting an already-connected goal is a success with already_connected:true, saved:false and a note, and nothing is saved, avoiding the duplicate the raw engine call would create. An unknown goal or out-of-range solver_index is an error. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Content path to the IK Rig asset. |
| `goal_name` | string | yes | Name of an existing goal (created via add_ik_goal). |
| `solver_index` | number | yes | Index of the solver in the rig's solver stack. |

**Returns:** `{ ik_rig_path: string, goal_name: string, solver_index: int, connected: bool, already_connected: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `copy_anim_graph_nodes`

*Additive.*

Copy a set of AnimGraph nodes (with internal FAnimNode settings + intra-selection wiring) between graphs. Equivalent to the editor's copy/paste: preserves each node's runtime struct properties and any links WITHIN the copied set (links to nodes outside the selection are dropped). Saves the destination ABP but does NOT recompile it -- run compile_anim_blueprint after your edits for runtime effect.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src_anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Source UAnimBlueprint path/name. |
| `node_ids` | array | yes | Array of source NodeGuid strings (from get_graph_nodes) to copy. |
| `dst_anim_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Destination UAnimBlueprint path/name. |
| `src_graph` | string | no | Source graph name (optional, default the top-level AnimGraph). |
| `dst_graph` | string | no | Destination graph name (optional, default the top-level AnimGraph). |
| `offset_x` | number | no | X offset added to every pasted node (optional, default 0). |
| `offset_y` | number | no | Y offset added to every pasted node (optional, default 0). |

**Returns:** `{ copied_count, id_map:{old->new}, imported_nodes[], missing_node_ids[], saved }`

## `create_anim_blueprint`

*Additive.*

Create an Animation Blueprint (parent UAnimInstance) for a skeleton at package_path/name with the editor factory, compile it and save it; an existing Animation Blueprint at that path is returned unchanged (already_existed=true). Refused while PIE runs unless force=true. Returns asset_path, generated_class and target_skeleton_set.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package_path` | string | yes | UE content folder, e.g. /Game/MyGame |
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name for the new Animation Blueprint |
| `skeleton_path` | string | no | Optional skeleton path; defaults to /Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube_Skeleton |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, name: string, skeleton_path: string, generated_class: string, is_anim_instance: bool, target_skeleton_set: bool, created: bool, already_existed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `create_anim_composite`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create and save a UAnimComposite asset bound to a USkeleton, under /Game. Idempotent: a UAnimComposite already at that path is returned unchanged with already_existed=true and saved=false, and nothing is saved. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name (e.g. 'AnimComp_Example'). |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/Animation) |
| `skeleton_path` | string | no | Asset path of the target Skeleton |

**Returns:** `{ name, package_path, asset_path, composite_path, skeleton, num_segments, created, already_existed, saved, save_error, message }`

## `create_anim_montage`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create an empty-but-valid UAnimMontage asset at package_path/name, bound to skeleton_path, with a slot track named slot_name and a 'Default' section at time 0 but no animation yet, and save it; no undo transaction. Idempotent: a UAnimMontage already at that path is returned unchanged with already_existed=true and saved=false, even when its skeleton or slot differ, and nothing is saved; an asset of another class at that path is refused and nothing changes. Next, give it an animation with add_montage_segment, sections with add_montage_section and more slots with add_montage_slot, and read it back with get_montage_info. A skeleton_path that does not load is an error. A failed save (always while PIE runs) makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name, no folder or extension, e.g. 'AM_Attack'. |
| `package_path` | string | no | Content folder as a long package path, e.g. '/Game/Animation/Montages' (default /Game/Animation; a trailing slash is ignored). |
| `slot_name` | string | no | Name of the slot track the montage plays on, e.g. 'DefaultSlot' or 'UpperBody' (default DefaultSlot); the AnimBlueprint must have a Slot node with that name to play it. |
| `skeleton_path` | string | no | Object path of the USkeleton the montage plays on, e.g. '/Game/Characters/SK_Hero_Skeleton' (default the engine's /Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube_Skeleton). |

**Returns:** `{ name, package_path, asset_path, montage_path, skeleton_path, slot_names, slot_name, slot_count, section_count, created, already_existed, saved, save_error, message }`

## `create_anim_sequence`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create a UAnimSequence at package_path/anim_name bound to the USkeleton at skeleton_path (default the engine SkeletalCube_Skeleton) and save it; its data model gets frame_rate rounded to whole fps and round(length_seconds * fps) frames, but no bone tracks or curves. Idempotent: a UAnimSequence already at that path is returned unchanged (already_existed=true, saved=false, length and rate not applied) and nothing is saved; another asset class there or an unknown skeleton is an error. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, and the new asset stays in memory only. Fill it with set_anim_bone_track_keys (identity keys when keys is omitted) or add_anim_float_curve; inspect it with get_anim_sequence_info.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anim_name` | string | yes | Asset name (no path). |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/MCP) |
| `length_seconds` | number | no | Sequence length in seconds (default 1.0) |
| `frame_rate` | number | no | Sampling frame rate in fps (default 30) |
| `skeleton_path` | string | no | Asset path of the target Skeleton |

**Returns:** `{ anim_sequence_path, anim_name, skeleton, play_length, frame_rate, num_frames, success, saved, save_error, already_existed, message }`

## `create_blend_space`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create and save a blend space asset under /Game -- a 2D UBlendSpace (default), a UBlendSpace1D, or an aim offset (UAimOffsetBlendSpace or UAimOffsetBlendSpace1D) picked by blend_space_type -- and write every axis setting it is given (name, range and grid divisions of the X axis, and of the Y axis on a 2D type) before rebuilding its runtime data. Idempotent: a blend space already at that path is returned unchanged with already_existed=true and saved=false, and nothing is written or saved (blend_space_type then reports the class it already has). An unknown blend_space_type, one that contradicts is_1d, an axis minimum not below its maximum, a grid below 1 or a Y-axis param on a 1D type is refused before anything is created. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name (e.g. 'BS_Example'). |
| `asset_name` | string | no | Alias of name. |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/Animation) |
| `blend_space_type` | string | no | Optional class to create: BlendSpace (2D, default) \| BlendSpace1D \| AimOffset (2D UAimOffsetBlendSpace) \| AimOffset1D (UAimOffsetBlendSpace1D), any case. Omitted, is_1d picks BlendSpace1D or BlendSpace. |
| `is_1d` | boolean | no | If true create a 1D BlendSpace, else 2D (default false); when blend_space_type is also given they must agree. |
| `axis_name` | string | no | X-axis display name (default 'Speed'; 'Yaw' for an aim offset) |
| `axis_min` | number | no | X-axis minimum value (default 0; -90 for an aim offset); must be below axis_max. |
| `min_value` | number | no | Alias of axis_min. |
| `axis_max` | number | no | X-axis maximum value (default 100; 90 for an aim offset) |
| `max_value` | number | no | Alias of axis_max. |
| `axis_grid` | number | no | Optional X-axis grid divisions, an integer >= 1 (default: the engine's 4). |
| `num_grid_points` | number | no | Alias of axis_grid. |
| `y_axis_name` | string | no | Optional Y-axis display name, 2D types only (default 'Pitch' for an aim offset; otherwise the engine's 'None' is kept). |
| `y_axis_min` | number | no | Optional Y-axis minimum, 2D types only (default 0; -90 for an aim offset); must be below y_axis_max. |
| `y_axis_max` | number | no | Optional Y-axis maximum, 2D types only (default 100; 90 for an aim offset). |
| `y_axis_grid` | number | no | Optional Y-axis grid divisions, 2D types only, an integer >= 1 (default: the engine's 4). |
| `skeleton_path` | string | no | Asset path of the target Skeleton (default /Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube_Skeleton) |

**Returns:** `{ name, package_path, asset_path, blend_space_path, blend_space_type, is_1d, skeleton_path, axis_name, axis_min, axis_max, axis_grid_num, y_axis_name?, y_axis_min?, y_axis_max?, y_axis_grid_num?, sample_count, created, already_existed, saved, save_error, message }`

## `create_control_rig_blueprint`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create a Control Rig Blueprint (non-modular) at package_path/name with UControlRigBlueprintFactory, compile it and save it. Idempotent: an existing Control Rig Blueprint there is returned unchanged (already_existed=true). Returns asset_path, generated_class, is_control_rig and saved; refused while PIE runs unless force is set.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package_path` | string | yes | Content folder starting with "/", e.g. "/Game/Rigs"; a trailing slash is ignored |
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name of the Control Rig Blueprint, e.g. "CR_Hero" |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, name: string, generated_class: string, is_control_rig: bool, created: bool, already_existed: bool, saved: bool, save_error: string }`

## `create_editable_skeleton`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create a USkeleton at package_path/name by duplicating an existing skeleton (default /Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube_Skeleton), then save it, so add_bone, set_bone_transform, add_virtual_bone and the other bone tools edit a project copy instead of engine content. Idempotent by path: a skeleton already there is returned untouched with created=false and saved=false. A package_path that does not start with a slash, a source that does not exist or is not a skeleton, or another kind of asset at the target is an error, and nothing is created. A failed save, as during PIE, makes success false with save_error and keeps the new skeleton in memory. A mesh to go with it: duplicate_asset on a skeletal mesh (destination_path); inspect the result: get_skeleton_info (load_full_data=true).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package_path` | string | yes | UE content folder starting with a slash, e.g. /Game/MyGame |
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name for the new skeleton, e.g. "SK_Creature_Skeleton"; with package_path it gives the asset path. |
| `source_skeleton` | string | no | Asset path of the skeleton to duplicate, e.g. "/Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube_Skeleton", which is also the default. |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, name: string, source: string, bone_count: int, created: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `create_ik_retargeter`

*Additive.*

Create and save a UIKRetargeter asset wiring source + target IK Rigs. An existing retargeter at that path is rewired and saved when either rig differs; when it already uses both rigs nothing changes, nothing is saved (saved=false) and a note says so. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package_path` | string | yes | UE content folder, e.g. /Game/MyGame |
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name for the new IK Retargeter |
| `source_ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the source UIKRigDefinition (copy FROM) |
| `target_ik_rig_path` | string | yes | Path to the target UIKRigDefinition (copy TO) |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, name: string, source_ik_rig: string, target_ik_rig: string, created: bool, already_existed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `create_ik_rig`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create and save a UIKRigDefinition asset and set its source skeletal mesh.  Idempotent: an existing rig is loaded and only given the mesh, then saved, when it has another one; when it already has that mesh, or the mesh does not load or the engine refuses it (skeletal_mesh_set false), nothing changes, nothing is saved and a note says why. The default skeletal_mesh_path is /Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package_path` | string | yes | UE content folder, e.g. /Game/MyGame |
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name for the new IK Rig |
| `skeletal_mesh_path` | string | no | Optional USkeletalMesh asset path; defaults to /Engine/EngineMeshes/SkeletalCube |

**Returns:** `{ asset_path: string, name: string, skeletal_mesh: string, skeletal_mesh_set: bool, created: bool, already_existed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `create_locomotion_anim_blueprint`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create in one call an Animation Blueprint for a skeleton with a locomotion state machine: the machine, its states (Idle, Walk, Run by default), the entry wired to the first state and a transition each way between consecutive states, then compile and save it. Use it as the quick start for a character; for any other layout build the machine from a JSON spec with build_anim_state_machine, or step by step with create_anim_blueprint, add_anim_state_machine, add_anim_state and add_anim_transition. What it leaves to do: the states are empty (put an animation in each with add_anim_graph_node) and the transitions have no rule, so they are never taken (set_anim_transition_rule_from_comparison, _from_bool or _automatic). Idempotent: an existing Animation Blueprint, machine, state or transition is reused, not duplicated, and an entry already wired is left alone; an existing blueprint is kept even if its skeleton is not skeleton_path. Compile errors are not reported here (check with compile_anim_blueprint); a failed save is an error. Refused while PIE runs unless force=true.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package_path` | string | yes | Content folder for the asset, e.g. "/Game/Characters/Hero/Animation" (a trailing slash is ignored). |
| `asset_name` | string | yes | Name of the Animation Blueprint, e.g. "ABP_Hero"; the asset is package_path/asset_name. |
| `skeleton_path` | string | yes | Path of the USkeleton asset, e.g. "/Game/Characters/Hero/SK_Hero_Skeleton"; it must load even when the blueprint already exists. |
| `machine_name` | string | no | Name of the state machine node in the AnimGraph (default "Locomotion"); a machine of that name is reused. |
| `states` | array | no | State names in order, e.g. ["Idle", "Walk", "Run", "Sprint"] (default ["Idle", "Walk", "Run"]); the first is the entry state, and transitions link each state with the next one. |
| `add_transitions` | boolean | no | Whether to add the two-way transitions between consecutive states, with a 0.2 s crossfade (default true); false leaves the states unlinked. |

**Returns:** `{ anim_blueprint_path, package_path, skeleton_path, machine_name, state_count, transition_count, entry_wired, entry_state, note_states_are_empty, already_existed, saved, save_error? }`

## `create_pose_asset`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create an empty UPoseAsset (no poses) at package_path/name, bound to the USkeleton at skeleton_path (default the engine SkeletalCube_Skeleton), and save it; no undo transaction. Idempotent: a UPoseAsset already at that path is returned untouched with already_existed=true and saved=false, even when bound to another skeleton, and nothing is saved. A name taken by another asset class or an unknown skeleton is an error, and a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Add poses with add_pose_to_pose_asset; to build one from animation frames use create_pose_asset_from_anim_sequence.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name (e.g. 'Pose_Example'). |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content package path where the asset is created (default /Game/Animation) |
